experimental_method: Vibrating-tube densimetry under flow: density difference between gas-free water and water saturated with the gas at about 100 kPa and 298.15 K gives the partial molar volume at infinite dilution, using Henry's-law mole fraction from the literature.
uncertainties_stated: Maximum imprecision about +-1.5 cm3/mol (1.5-4 %); per-solute average deviation of replicates in the table; temperature +-0.002 K, pressure +-15 Pa, density precision a few ppm.
quality_remarks: Title printed with 'Gases' in quotes; PDF has 3 pages, all this paper. Partial molar volume at x2 < 1e-4 taken as infinite dilution value. Solute mole fraction x2 used in eq 4 was computed from literature Henry constants, so the result depends partly on literature data.
extraction_notes: Table I typed from the page image (text layer was scrambled by the two-column layout); plus-minus values split into value and uncertainty columns; blank literature cells for 9 solutes are empty. Sanity: all values 26-101 cm3/mol, plausible and increasing with molecular size.
